Subject: Post-demo: VPN jitter & concurrent streams — next steps
Attachments: demo-recording.mp4 (video), network-test-script.sh (bash)

Hi Megan and team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great walkthrough. Quick recap of the two items that popped as blockers for the Private deployment path and proposed next steps so we can scope a short verification window: 

Summary of observations from today's demo:
- Streaming behavior looked solid at low concurrency, but we saw intermittent packet reordering/jitter spikes at ~75 concurrent streams coming through the VPN tunnel.
- P95 end-to-end token latency drifted from ~220ms up to ~520ms during sustained bursts.
- The customer-side NAT timeouts and MTU fragmentation were likely contributors; our runtime also flagged occasional KV-cache miss amplification during retries.

What we need from Acme before the verification run:
1) Confirmation of VPN type and config: IPSec or AWS Transit Gateway? Any specific cipher/MSS settings?
2) Typical expected concurrent sessions from your upstream service (approx range).
3) A sample payload size and token rate (tokens/sec per stream) so we can simulate realistic traffic.
4) Permission for a 2-hour test window where Redwood will run synthetic streams from a dedicated test host (we can provide IPs).

Proposed Redwood acceptance targets for the test (we can adjust):
- P50 generation latency: <= 120ms
- P95 generation latency: <= 300ms under sustained 100 concurrent streams
- Maximum token-per-second per stream: 50 tokens/sec with sustained bursts up to 120 tokens/sec for 30s
- No more than 1% failed stream resets attributable to network jitter during the window

Next steps / owners:
- Acme: share network-topology-diagram and confirm VPN details (Megan / netops)
- Redwood (Vanessa): prepare load script and test harness; will run the script in staging and share results
- Redwood (Ben): coordinate required firewall/IP whitelisting and provide test IPs

I attached the demo recording and the test script we plan to run. If the proposed test targets look off, tell us what you'd like instead and we'll align.

Thanks,

Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Mateo,

Appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers and notes from our side: 

Answers:
- VPN: Currently using IPSec tunnels terminated on our Palo Alto pair into an AWS TGW (we have two parallel tunnels for redundancy). MTU is default 1500; we've historically not adjusted MSS.
- Concurrent sessions: Our product produces bursts — typical steady state is 20-40 concurrent inference sessions, but during peak hour gateway traffic we can see 80-100 concurrent sessions for short periods.
- Payload: Typical request ~600 tokens (payload + expected response); token rate varies but average is ~30 tokens/sec per stream.

We are open to a 2-hour window next Wednesday 2026-10-20 between 10:00-12:00 PT. I attached a topology diagram and looped in netops so they can review rules. Two asks from our ops:
1) Please provide the test IPs and the exact time we will see traffic so we can stand up flow captures.
2) Give us an expected failure profile threshold so our on-call knows when to escalate during the test.

I'll defer to Vanessa on the exact script details, but the window above should work.

Thanks,
Megan
